prose.summary: The aluminium window frames meet the rule of origin under the India-UAE CEPA, so you can claim the preferential CEPA rate of 0% for your shipment to India. This reduces the normal duty rate from 10% to 0%, resulting in an estimated saving of 10000.00 AED for your shipment valued at 100000 AED. Please proceed with the checklist below to claim this preference.
prose.classification: The product is classified under Indian tariff line 76101000, which covers doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should still confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0% for this product. By claiming the CEPA rate, you can save an estimated 10000.00 AED on your shipment. Please note that the CEPA rate applies only to Basic Customs Duty, so other import charges such as IGST are still payable even when the CEPA rate is 0%.
prose.origin: To qualify for the CEPA rate, the product must meet the rule of origin, which requires a Change in Tariff Subheading (CTSH) and at least 45% Value Addition (VA). CTSH means that all non-originating inputs must be classified under a different 6-digit subheading than the final product, which was satisfied here. The Value Addition (VA) represents the share of the product's price that does not come from non-originating materials, calculated on an FOB basis. All checks passed: the final manufacture took place in the UAE, the work done exceeded minimal operations, the CTSH requirement was met, and the VA build-down reached 49.0%, which is above the 45% threshold.

notes.text: When filling out the certificate of origin, use box 9 for remarks as required by India's certificate form, because India's form governs entry into India, even though the agreement text mentions box 8.
The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only and is not the product-specific rule test for the CEPA, which is set per tariff line.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value, so actual duty amounts will differ from the estimate based on the shipment value given.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 via LiveLaw, taxmann), not confirmed in the official text.
The agreement says box 8 for remarks, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year record-keeping minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
The agreement does not define 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' used in the build-up method.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
